In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a composite of silicate and ice grains can fit the IRAS-LRS data.
the composite grains are the best candidates for circumstellar dust shells.

the observed IRAS–IRS curve for several circumstellar shells is consistent with the composite spheroid grain model with porosity and inhomogeneous distribution of inclusions of 0.5 – 0.7 μ m sized graphite and ices.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the composite grains with inclusions of voids or ices/graphites, with porosity and volume fractions of the inclusions, can be used to model the observed 10.0μ m feature.
composite grains with inclusions and porosities can explain the observed 10.0–12.0 μ m emission feature.
composite grains with inclusions and porosities are a possible candidate for the dust grains around evolved stars.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the observed IRAS– LRS curves can be reproduced with the help of composite grains.

the composite grains with porosity and inhomogeneity in the composition of the grain material can be used to explain the observed 10.0 – 10.5 μ m emission feature in the IRAS–LIRS spectra of several dust shells.
the composite grains with porosity and inhomogeneity of the dust can be used to explain the variation in the width of the observed 10.0 – 11.0 μ m features.
